mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces near-term discounting of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains > 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the tightening phase are not statistically lower than in the prior easing phase (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS decline is not persistent for > 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for a month, the S&P 500 is expected to underperform over the next 60 trading days due to investor anticipation of rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and holds above 3% for at least one month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the 60-day mean during the previous 2 years (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in PAYEMS labor cost index (> 2% month-over-month) coinciding with a decline in UNRATE suggests wage growth outpacing productivity, which predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% MoM and UNRATE decreases by > 0.5% MoM in the same month
failure_condition: Rank IC for this interaction < 0.05 over a 12-month window, or 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in INDPRO supply index (> 1.5%) while HOUST demand remains flat for two months predicts a temporary supply glut, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by > 1.5% and HOUST remains unchanged for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly lower than the prior 5-day average during similar supply expansion episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of double-digit month-over-month growth in GDPC1 personal consumption (e.g., +12%) indicate strong demand momentum that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 grows by > 10% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during such acceleration episodes are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in RSAFS Treasury demand (below 300 million) combined with a 1% monthly decline in UNRATE suggests financial market stress, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 300 and UNRATE decreases by > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during such events are not significantly negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months in a labor market expansion regime, it signals weaker labor constraints and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for three consecutive months and dominant_domain is labor expansion
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the UNRATE (below 5% for 4 months) coupled with a flat HOUST demand suggests weak demand-side pressure, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% for 4 consecutive months and HOUST remains flat for the same period
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during such episodes are not significantly lower than the 60-day mean of neutral regimes (p > 0.1).
